newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI says sees lower profit for year.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI says sees lower profit for year.

text.p: Nickel refiner QNI Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected profit for the current year to June 1997 to be lower than in 1995/96.

"As I mentioned earlier, the depressed market conditions which prevailed in the second half of the last financial year have continued into the first half of this current financial year with no signs of a recovery as yet," QNI chairman Max Roberts told shareholders at the annual general meeting.

"Accordingly, unless there is a marked improvement in market conditions with a related rise in nickel and cobalt prices, profit expectations for this year will not match last year's performance," Roberts said.
Roberts said the company was continuing the search for new long-term nickel ore supplies for its Yabulu refinery near Townsville on the Queensland coast.
He said exploration was focussed on the southwest Pacific region as well as the Philippines, Indonesia, and New Caledonia.

QNI was examining the potential development of Indonesian resources with Aneka Tambang and South Africa's Gencor Ltd and had plans for a new mining venture in New Caledonia, the source of its current supplies.
QNI's net profit fell to A$85.89 million in 1995/96 from A$107.19 million a year earlier.- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
